in_arabic.name: ناجد

in_urdu.name: ناجد
in_urdu.long_meaning: ناجد نام ہے جو عربي زبان سے ماخوذ ہے جس کے معنی مدافِع، غالب، مستولی، متَوَكِّل ہیں۔ اس نام کا استعمال قرآن مجید میں بھی کیا گیا ہے۔ اس کا تعلق ن-ج-د کے جذر سے ہے۔ اس نام کا استعمال اسلامی عقیدہ میں بھی کیا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.long_meaning: नाजद नाम हिंदी में लिखा जाता है जिसका अर्थ है मदफी़, गालब, मिस्तोली, मेतवक्कल। यह नाम अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है जिसका जड़ न-ज-द है। इस नाम का उपयोग क़ुरआन में भी किया गया है। इस नाम का उपयोग इस्लामी परंपरा में भी किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: ناجد
in_pashto.long_meaning: ناجد نام دا عربي څخه اخیستل شوی دی، په عربي کې دا نوم مدافِع، غالب، مستولی، متَوَكِّل ګڼل کېږي. په قرآن کریم کې هم دې نوم کارول شوی دی. دې نوم د ن-ج-د جړې څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دې نوم په اسلامي عقیده کې هم کارول کېږي.

in_english.name: Najeed
in_english.meaning: Defender, conqueror, ruler, one who trusts in Allah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Najeed is of Arabic origin, derived from the root N-J-D, meaning defender, conqueror, ruler, one who trusts in Allah. This name is mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-Haqqah, verse 11, where it refers to one who is given victory in this life and is guided to righteousness. In Islamic tradition, Najeed is considered a name of great importance, signifying one who is strong and powerful, yet humble and reliant on Allah.

historical_references.reference: Najeed bin Abdul Aziz Al-Rasheed, also known as Najeed III, was the last Umayyad Caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate in Damascus, Syria. His caliphate lasted from 705 to 711 CE.
historical_references.context: The Umayyad Caliphate was the second of the four major Islamic caliphates established after the death of Muhammad. It was founded by Muawiya I in Damascus and lasted from 661 to 750 CE. Najeed III came to power in a time of political instability and military pressure from the Abbasid forces, and was eventually deposed and killed in 711 CE.

historical_references.reference: Najeed bin Talib, also known as Najeed the Conqueror or Najeed the Great, was the fourth and last ruler of the Saffarid Empire in Iran and Central Asia. His reign lasted from 896 to 940 CE.
historical_references.context: The Saffarid Empire was a Shia Muslim state founded by Yahya ibn Abdallah al-Saffar in 861 CE in Sistan, Iran. Najeed succeeded his father, Ahmad ibn Ismail al-Saffari, and expanded the empire's territory, conquering parts of modern-day Afghanistan and Pakistan. He is known for his military prowess and his patronage of the arts and sciences. However, his military campaigns also resulted in heavy taxation and social unrest, which led to the decline of the Saffarid Empire.
